title: Reusable core session authentication seam
description: Objective: expose one reusable, fail-closed core decision for session, credential, proof-of-possession, replay, expiry, and transport authentication, then have authenticateCommand compose it before command capability admission. This is the prerequisite that lets daemon coordination authenticate a session without fabricating a RuntimeCommandEnvelope or forking core precedence. NOT in scope: choosing a cryptographic proof algorithm, persistence, daemon wiring, recipient/effect registries, or coordination mailbox behavior. Owned paths: packages/core/src/identity/authenticate-session.ts, packages/core/src/identity/authenticate-session.js, packages/core/src/identity/authenticate-session.test.ts, packages/core/src/identity/authenticate-command.ts, packages/core/src/index.ts. Production consumer: Durable daemon session and coordination-recipient authority, then task-4afcb06422ed4adb89430b7ea9758d7f. Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/core typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/core test && pnpm typecheck.
definitionOfDone: A frozen reusable session-authentication result validates the committed principal, session, credential, presented proof, verifier result, replay result, expiry, generation, client key, and transport facts without accepting caller-supplied positive booleans as authority.

Every refusal preserves the exact stable core code and refusing layer with AUTHENTICATION_FAILED before SESSION_REPLAYED before SESSION_EXPIRED, returns zero principal/session authority, and UNKNOWN or malformed verifier/replay evidence denies.

authenticateCommand delegates session authentication to the new production seam and only then applies its existing exact RuntimeCommand capability check; its public behavior and existing tests remain byte-for-byte compatible.

Focused tests cover success and every refusal/precedence branch, assert code plus layer and zero-authority output, assert generated-case counts, and mutation-drill each production guard so bypassing it turns the focused test red.
The exact verification command exits 0 and the daemon authority prerequisite is named as the real consumer; no proof algorithm, persistence, or coordination capability mapping is introduced here.
taskRails: Keep the core decision pure and dependency-free; injected proof/replay observations are evidence inputs, never inferred truth.
Do not add coordination endpoint strings to RuntimeCommandKind or synthesize fake runtime commands.
Preserve all existing identity authentication reason codes, layers, and precedence.

implementationPlan.description: Measure and pin the baseline before editing. Run `pnpm --filter @moe/core test` and record file/test counts (measured 2026-08-09: 16 files / 239 tests passing). Read packages/core/src/identity/authenticate-command.ts end to end and write down its EXACT current refusal order, which is the contract this task must preserve byte-for-byte: (1) bindingsHold false -> AUTHENTICATION_FAILED; (2) verifyProof throws OR returns !== true -> AUTHENTICATION_FAILED; (3) checkReplay throws OR returns a value that is neither "FRESH" nor "REPLAYED" -> AUTHENTICATION_FAILED; (4) replay === "REPLAYED" OR !isCurrentGeneration(session, credential) -> SESSION_REPLAYED; (5) session.status !== "ACTIVE" -> SESSION_REPLAYED; (6) !isSessionUsableAt(session, now) -> SESSION_EXPIRED; (7) !session.transportIds.includes(transportId) -> CAPABILITY_DENIED; (8) capability match / step-up window -> CAPABILITY_DENIED. Guards 1-7 move to the new seam. Guard 8 (matchCapability + STEP_UP_WINDOW) STAYS in authenticateCommand and is not touched. Do not start editing until this list is written down; it is the acceptance oracle for every later step.

implementationPlan.description: Implement packages/core/src/identity/authenticate-session.ts to turn the tests green. Export: SESSION_AUTH_LAYERS = Object.freeze(["BINDING","PROOF","REPLAY","GENERATION","SESSION_STATE","EXPIRY","TRANSPORT"] as const); type SessionAuthLayer; type SessionAuthCode = "AUTHENTICATION_FAILED" | "SESSION_REPLAYED" | "SESSION_EXPIRED" | "CAPABILITY_DENIED"; interface AuthenticatedSessionFacts { principalId, principalKind, profileRevisionId, sessionId, clientKeyId, projectId, transportId }; SessionAuthenticationResult = { ok: true; facts: AuthenticatedSessionFacts } | { ok: false; code: SessionAuthCode; layer: SessionAuthLayer } — the refusal arm carries NO facts field at all, so zero authority is a type-level guarantee, not a convention. MOVE PresentedProof, ProofChallenge and ReplayOutcome here verbatim from authenticate-command.ts (they are envelope-independent). Input is SessionAuthenticationInput: principal, session, credential, projectId, transportId, now, requestId, requestDigest, presentedCredentialId, proof, verifyProof, checkReplay. requestId/requestDigest/presentedCredentialId are the three scalars authenticateCommand currently reads off the envelope (commandId, requestDigest, sessionCredential) — this is exactly how a non-command caller authenticates without fabricating a RuntimeCommandEnvelope (task rail 2). Port bindingsHold unchanged except that the three envelope reads become those scalars, and add isNonEmpty checks on requestId/requestDigest/presentedCredentialId since there is no envelope decoder upstream to have validated them. Rebuild the ProofChallenge from records only ({ commandId: requestId, requestDigest, credentialId: credential.credentialId, clientKeyId: session.clientKeyId }) and never read input.proof past bindingsHold, preserving the existing defence against a caller-attached verified flag. Wrap verifyProof and checkReplay in try/catch; a throw or any non-"FRESH"/"REPLAYED" value denies (UNKNOWN never authorizes, epic rail 4). Import only from ./identity-session.js — no @moe/contracts, no createRuntimeError; the seam returns a code string and the caller maps it (task rail 1: pure and dependency-free). Freeze both result arms. Also create the bridge packages/core/src/identity/authenticate-session.js containing EXACTLY the bytes `export * from "./authenticate-session.ts";` plus a single LF — runtime-entrypoint.test.ts compares bridge bytes through utf8 and a CRLF ending fails there while git diff --stat shows nothing. AMEND-1 APPLIED CORRECTLY AND NOT LOOSENED — the specific thing the reopen said to check. `expect(REFUSAL_CASES).toHaveLength(10)` is an **exact** count, not `>= 9`. `Object.isFrozen(REFUSAL_CASES)` is asserted. And the layer assertion is stronger than the count: `expect([...new Set(REFUSAL_CASES.map(({layer}) => layer))]).toEqual([...SESSION_AUTH_LAYERS])` compares the distinct layers against the **production** constant, in order. A case list that dropped a layer, or a production layer with no case, both redden. That is the "assert the case list, not just the case count" property in its strong form.

DoD 2's PRECEDENCE CLAUSE — I could not find it by grep and settled it by mutation instead of by assumption. My grep for `preced|before|simultaneous|both|wins|first` returned nothing, which is exactly the point at which a reviewer either shrugs or rejects on absence. The governor asked whether this task's seam is where the daemon HTTP Authenticator's policy belongs. It is not, and the reason is structural rather than stylistic. apps/daemon/src/http/http-contract.ts:110 declares `authenticate(credential: string | null)`. http-adapter.ts calls it at line 154; decodeRuntimeCommandEnvelopeBytes runs at line 163. The documented pipeline at http-adapter.ts:33 is `authenticate -> compatibility -> bounded decode -> registry -> authorize`, and the contract comment states the ordering exists so attacker bytes are never decoded for an unauthenticated caller. A PRE-DECODE gate cannot supply commandId, requestDigest or a proof-of-possession — those only exist after decoding. authenticateSession requires all three. So the HTTP port is a cheap transport-credential gate that necessarily runs BEFORE the facts this seam consumes exist. Collapsing them would force decoding untrusted bytes before authentication, which is the exact inversion the daemon boundary was built to prevent. task-8470a860 is therefore NOT named as a consumer, and nobody should later merge these two on the grounds that both are 'authentication'.
